Why do cows wear bells? Because their horns do not work! Moo!
What is a cat's favourite colour? Purr-ple! Meow!
Why did the teddy bear say no to dessert? Because he was already stuffed!
What do you call a fish with no eyes? A fsh! Ha ha!
Why are frogs so happy? Because they eat whatever bugs them!
What did the zero say to the eight? Nice belt!

What kind of tree fits in your hand? A palm tree!

riddles.q: I have a long trunk, big ears, and I am very big. Who am I?
I say moo, and I give you milk. Who am I?
I am yellow, I am long, and monkeys love to eat me. What am I?
I shine in the sky during the day, and I keep you warm. What am I?
I have four legs, I wag my tail, and I say woof. Who am I?
I come after rain, and I have seven colours. What am I?
I have hands, but I cannot clap. I tell you the time. What am I?
I am full of water, I fall from clouds. What am I?
I hop, hop, hop, and I say ribbit. Who am I?
You wear me on your feet when you go outside. What am I?

faq.a: Sunlight has all the colours of the rainbow in it. When it bumps into the air, the blue light bounces around the most, so the whole sky looks blue!
Leaves and grass have a special green helper inside them that catches sunlight to make food for the plant. That helper is green!
The sun warms up water, and it floats up into the sky as tiny drops. They join together to make clouds. When the clouds get too heavy, the water falls down as rain!

q: why do i have to sleep
faq.a: When we sleep, our body and brain rest and grow. Sleep gives us energy to play and learn tomorrow!

q: where does the sun go at night
faq.a: The sun does not go anywhere! Our Earth slowly spins around. When our side turns away from the sun, it becomes night for us.

q: why is the moon changing shape
faq.a: The moon does not really change. We see different parts of it lit by the sun, so sometimes it looks round and sometimes like a banana!
Birds have light bones and strong wings with feathers. They flap their wings to push the air, and up they go!

q: why do we brush our teeth
why should i brush my teeth
faq.a: Brushing cleans away tiny germs and bits of food, so our teeth stay strong and shiny!
Vegetables have vitamins that help us grow tall and strong, and help us fight off coughs and colds!
A rainbow happens when sunlight shines through raindrops. The drops split the light into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet!
Cats purr when they feel happy and cozy. It is like a cat's way of smiling!
Fish eat tiny plants, little bugs, and special fish food. Some big fish eat smaller fish.

q: why do we have to wash our hands
faq.a: Our hands pick up tiny germs we cannot see. Washing with soap and water sends the germs away, so we stay healthy!
The sun is very, very big! More than a million Earths could fit inside it. It looks small because it is so far away.
The blue whale is the biggest animal ever. It is longer than two buses!
The cheetah is the fastest animal on land. It can run as fast as a car on the highway!
Stars are giant suns, very, very far away. They seem to twinkle because their light wiggles as it travels through our air.
That is a lovely question! Babies grow in a special place inside their mummy's tummy. Your family can tell you more about it.
Bones are like a strong frame inside our body. They help us stand, walk, and keep our heart and brain safe.
Rivers carry tiny bits of salt from rocks into the sea. The salt stays there, so the sea is salty!

q: how many legs does a spider have
faq.a: A spider has eight legs. Insects, like ants and bees, have only six legs.

q: how many legs does an insect have
how many legs does an ant have
faq.a: Insects, like ants, bees and butterflies, have six legs.
Jupiter is the biggest planet. It is so big that more than a thousand Earths could fit inside it!
The giraffe is the tallest animal. Its long neck helps it eat leaves from the top of tall trees.
Mount Everest is the tallest mountain in the world. It is so high that it has snow on top all year.
Dogs bark to talk! A bark can mean hello, I am excited, or someone is at the door.
The sun is so bright that it looks yellow or white. Never look straight at the sun, because it can hurt your eyes.
The moon is grey, with dark patches. At night it looks silvery white, because sunlight bounces off it.
The moon is round, like a ball. Sometimes only part of it is lit up by the sun, so it can look like a banana!
The sun is round, like a giant glowing ball.
The Earth is round, like a big ball. It is so big that it looks flat when we stand on it.
I like blue, like the sky and the sea! What is your favourite colour?
I don't eat food, because I'm a little computer. I run on electricity! What is your favourite food?
I like elephants, because they are big, gentle and very clever. Which animal do you like?
I'm Buddy, a little talking computer. I'm not a person, and I'm not alive, but I love to learn and play with you!
I live right here, inside this little box! I'm happy to be here with you.
A team of people made me, to help children learn and have fun.
No, I can't see. I don't have eyes, but I can hear you when you talk to me.
I don't know your name yet, but I know you're my friend!

topics.say: Stars are giant balls of hot, glowing gas, very, very far away. Our sun is a star too! On a dark night, we can see lots of stars twinkling in the sky.
The sun is a star, and it is the closest star to us. It gives us light and keeps us warm, and plants need sunshine to grow. Never look straight at the sun, because it can hurt your eyes.
The moon is a big ball of rock that goes around our Earth. It does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight bounces off it. Astronauts have walked on the moon!
Earth is our home planet. It is a big round ball, covered with land and lots of blue ocean. Earth goes all the way around the sun once every year.
Planets are big round worlds that go around the sun. There are eight of them, and Earth is one. The biggest planet is Jupiter, and the one closest to the sun is Mercury.
Space is everything far above our sky, where the stars and planets are. There is no air to breathe in space, so astronauts wear special suits and helmets.
A rocket is a machine that flies up into space. It pushes hot gas out of the bottom very, very fast, and whoosh, up it goes!
The sky is the air all around and above us. In the day it looks blue, and at night it gets dark, so we can see the moon and the stars.
Clouds are made of lots and lots of tiny drops of water, floating high in the sky. When the drops join together and get too heavy, they fall down as rain.
Rain is water falling from the clouds. Rain fills up rivers and lakes, and it gives plants and animals the water they need.
A rainbow is a colourful arch in the sky. You can see one when the sun shines while it is raining. It has seven colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
Snow is frozen water that falls from the clouds when it is very cold. Each snowflake is a tiny piece of ice. You can make a snowman with snow!
Ice is water that has frozen because it got very cold. When ice gets warm, it melts and turns back into water.
Wind is air that is moving. We cannot see it, but we can feel it on our face, and we can see it move the trees and fly our kites.
Lightning is a giant spark of electricity in the clouds, and thunder is the loud boom it makes. When there is a storm, stay inside with a grown-up, where it is safe.
Our Earth spins around, like a slow top. When our side faces the sun, it is day. When our side turns away from the sun, it is night, and time to sleep.
All living things need water: people, animals and plants. Drinking water helps your body stay healthy, so remember to drink some every day!
The ocean is a huge, deep sea of salty water. It covers most of our Earth. Whales, dolphins, fish, octopuses and crabs all live in the ocean.
A river is water that flows across the land, all the way to the sea. Fish live in rivers, and people use river water for drinking and for farms.
A mountain is a very, very tall hill made of rock. The tallest mountain in the world is Mount Everest. It is so high that it has snow on top all year.
A volcano is a special mountain with an opening at the top. Deep inside, the rock is so hot that it melts. Sometimes the hot melted rock, called lava, comes out!
Fire is very hot and gives light. Grown-ups use it to cook food. Fire can burn us, so never touch fire or play with matches. Always stay safe!
Trees are big plants with strong wooden trunks. They give us shade, fruit and fresh air, and they are homes for birds and squirrels.
Flowers are the colourful parts of plants. Bees and butterflies visit them to drink a sweet juice called nectar. Many flowers later turn into fruits and seeds.
Plants grow from tiny seeds. To grow big and strong, a plant needs water, sunlight, air and good soil.
Fruits like apples, bananas and mangoes are sweet and healthy. They have vitamins that keep us strong. Fruits grow on plants and trees, and they hold the seeds inside.
The mango is a sweet, juicy fruit that grows on mango trees. In India it is called the king of fruits! Mangoes are ready to eat in summer.
Healthy food helps us grow. Vegetables, fruits, dal, rice and milk give our body energy. Eating food of many different colours every day is a great idea!
A butterfly starts life as a tiny caterpillar. The caterpillar eats lots of leaves, then wraps itself up and changes into a butterfly with beautiful wings.
Ants are tiny insects that live together in big groups. They work as a team, and an ant can carry things much heavier than itself!
A spider has eight legs. Spiders spin silky webs to catch little insects to eat. A spider is not an insect, because insects have only six legs.
Rabbits have long ears and strong back legs for hopping. They love to munch on grass, leaves and carrots, and they live in burrows under the ground.
Fish live in water. They breathe with special parts called gills, and they swim by moving their tails and fins. Some fish are tiny, and some are very big!

Dinosaurs were animals that lived a very, very long time ago, long before people. Some were as big as a house, and some were as small as a chicken. We know about them from their bones, called fossils.
Your heart is a strong muscle inside your chest. It pumps blood all around your body, all day and all night. Put your hand on your chest. Can you feel it go thump, thump?
Your brain is inside your head. It helps you think, learn, remember and feel. It tells every part of your body what to do!
A train is a long line of carriages pulled by an engine. Trains run on metal tracks, and they carry lots of people and things from one city to another.
A car has four wheels and an engine, and it takes people from place to place on roads. Always wear your seat belt in the car, to stay safe!
A bus is a big vehicle that carries lots of people at the same time. Many children ride a bus to school.
An aeroplane flies high in the sky, with big wings and strong engines. It can carry people far away, even to other countries, very fast.
Boats and ships float on water. Small boats can be rowed with oars, and big ships have engines. They carry people and things across rivers and seas.
A kite is light, and the wind pushes it up into the sky. You hold the long string, and the kite dances in the wind!
A computer is a machine that follows instructions very, very fast. It can help us write, draw, and find things out. I am a little computer too!
A robot is a machine that can do jobs by itself, because people taught it what to do. Some robots help build cars, and some even explore other planets!
Gravity is an invisible pull. The Earth pulls everything down towards it. That is why a ball falls down when you drop it, and why we don't float away!
School is where children learn to read, write and count, and make new friends. Teachers help us learn new things every day.
Books are full of stories and facts. When you read a book, or someone reads it to you, you can learn about anything, even dinosaurs and space!
A friend is someone you like to play with, who is kind to you. Good friends share, take turns, and help each other.
A family is the people who love you and take care of you, like your mummy, daddy, grandparents, brothers and sisters.
A doctor helps people when they are sick or hurt. Doctors check our body, and help us feel better and stay healthy.
